name: Made Here!

pick.label: Pick a product
pick.heading: Pick an import and make it at home
lead: Almost everything we use every day travels a long way to reach us: bananas from Ecuador, trainers from Vietnam, phones from China. Plenty of politicians would love to bring the making back home.

Choose something Germany hardly ever makes and start making it here, as close to Berlin as you can manage. Here are some ideas, but you can choose your own. *Bonus points for anything grown in Brandenburg in February.*
pick.hint: Or click one to choose it.
pick.note: Obviously I am not looking for a serious business plan. Some of these could almost work, and some would need a greenhouse the size of Tempelhof. Both are welcome.

rows: What are you going to start making at home?
Guess if you don’t know. Which country, how far, and by ship, plane or lorry?
Where, with what, and who does the work? A factory, a greenhouse, a garage in Neukölln…
The price, compared with the import:
Twice as much? Ten times? Be honest.
Who buys it anyway, and why? Pride, quality, the planet, showing off?
What it says on the label:
The name, the slogan, the little flag…

values.now: Mostly Ecuador and Colombia, about 10,000 kilometres away, on refrigerated ships. They’re picked green and ripened in special rooms when they get here, which I only found out last week.
values.how: Tempelhof Bananas: a giant heated greenhouse in one of the old hangars at Tempelhof, warmed by the waste heat from a data centre next door. The pickers get free banana bread.
values.price: About four euros a banana. Possibly five in winter.
values.buyers: People in Prenzlauer Berg who already pay six euros for a flat white, and restaurants that want to write “Berlin bananas” on the menu.
values.label: A banana in a little Berlin bear costume. The slogan: “Krumm, aber von hier.” (Bent, but from round here.)

yours.label: Your product
yours.heading: Your idea
yours.lead: Fill it in on your own phone or laptop (it stays on your device), and be ready to tell the class about your product in a few sentences.

rank.label: The ranking
rank.heading: Which product wins?
rank.lead: Each student tells us about their product in a few sentences. Add it, then argue it into place: the one you would actually buy at the top, the one only a government minister would buy at the bottom.
